title: Tiered degradation, KV slimming, and cold-start retry protocol for GPU OOM resilience
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: We occasionally see transient OOM spikes during sustained continuous-batching workloads and during model swap/cold-start transitions. Current mitigation (eviction + model fallback) is too blunt: it either kills sessions or forces full model fallback which causes latency/quality cliffs. Goal: implement a layered, memory-pressure aware protocol that performs 'KV slimming' (compact/trim hot KV entries instead of full eviction), progressive fidelity degradation across compatible model variants, and a cold-start retry protocol that avoids OOM storms during model loads. The feature should preserve latency SLOs where possible, keep quality regressions bounded, and provide clear observability for debug and postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: KV slimming implemented in runtime: compact and trim policies available behind flag
Batch admission rejects/accepts using pressure score and performs token-trimming heuristics when necessary
Progressive fidelity degradation pipeline implemented: FP32 -> 8-bit quantized variant -> smaller architecture -> shortened max_output and token-sampling fallback
Cold-start retry protocol implemented: exponential backoff + staggered admission for warmup without mass eviction
Ops runbook updated and dashboard panels added showing KV size distribution, memory pressure score, fallback activations, and per-tenant quality regression metrics
proposed_solution: 1) Memory-pressure metric: combine free_gpu_memory_percent, active_kv_bytes, queued_batch_tokens -> single pressure score. 2) KV slimming: when pressure above soft threshold, mark least-recently-used sessions for slimming. Slimming actions: a) compact in-memory KV to 8-bit where possible; b) trim prefix tokens using LRU heuristics; c) serialize cold session KV to compressed on-disk cache (if configured) with async eviction. 3) Batch admission: admission controller computes post-admit pressure; if admit would cross hard threshold, attempt KV slimming for candidate sessions and re-evaluate. 4) Progressive fidelity pipeline: define ordered compatible variants per model (e.g., llama-2-70b-fp32 -> llama-2-70b-8bit -> llama-2-13b-8bit); route an affected request to a lower-fidelity variant with user-visible signal (X-degraded: true) and optional short explanation. 5) Cold-start retry protocol: when loading a model, stagger worker activation, use short admission windows for warmup, and enforce a reserved emergency_kv_slab that is never reclaimed except for preemptive retries. 6) Retry semantics: idempotent requests may be retried once automatically after fallback; non-idempotent requests surface a 429 with guidance. 7) Observability: trace tags for slimming/fallback events, sampling of session-level quality diffs, and SLO guards for degradation frequency.
milestones: M2: KV slimming primitives (compaction + trimming) + unit tests (2026-03-15)
M3: Progressive fidelity routing + compatibility map + integration tests (2026-03-20)
M4: Cold-start retry protocol + e2e, canary rollout to staging (2026-03-24)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike experiments showed 28% reduction in peak GPU KV allocation when compressing to 8-bit for inactive sessions (testbed: a100-80gb, batch mix A)
2026-03-04: Prototype admission controller integrated into staging; observed an edge case where slimming caused CPU pressure—added async background compaction to mitigate
2026-03-07: Compatibility mapping created for top 12 models; found 2 models lacking a safe quantized variant — flagged for research to produce a fast fallback transformer proxy
2026-03-09: Canary load test with progressive-fidelity: median latency increased 12ms for degraded requests but 95th percentile latency improved because model fallback prevented queue blowups
2026-03-10: Added emergency_kv_slab reserve of 6% per-GPU; initial canary shows no OOMs on a 72-hour stress run with mixed traffic
test_plan: Unit tests for kv-slimming primitives (compress/decompress correctness, trimming semantics)
Integration tests for admission controller under synthetic memory pressure scenarios
Chaos tests: simulate model load & worker flapping to verify cold-start retry avoids cascading OOMs
Canary: 1% traffic in staging world with realism traces and per-tenant monitoring for fallback rates and quality regressions
observability_and_slos: New metrics: runtime.memory_pressure_score, kv_slim_events_total, fallback_variant_rate, cold_start_retry_count
Dashboards: KV size distribution, per-session trimming heatmap, fallback quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE proxies), SLO: fallback rate < 0.5% per-customer per-day
Alerting: alert if fallback_variant_rate > 1% (P0) or cold_start_retry_count spikes > baseline by 5x (P1)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV compression increases CPU and serialization latency -> Mitigation: do compaction asynchronously and limit compaction concurrency
Risk: Quality regression from smaller variants -> Mitigation: limit progressive degradation to low-latency-tolerant routes and expose AB test flags per-customer
Risk: Race during cold-start when many workers attach -> Mitigation: stagger activation + emergency_kv_slab + backoff token admission
notes: Design review 2026-03-05: PM asked for explicit per-tenant opt-out; added config: tenant.degradation_policy = opt-in|opt-out|auto
Operations request: add migration path for customers using on-prem disk-cache when enabling serialization of cold KV
Implementation note: prefer vectorized SIMD compression kernels to reduce CPU overhead; research team to validate quantization quality for KV tensors by 2026-03-12
